question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the percentage of India's population that live in urban areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.16%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, 31.16% of India's population lived in urban areas, while the remaining 68.84% lived in rural areas. (जनगणना 2011 — शहरी जनसंख्या 31.16%)

 

• The total population of India in 2011 was about 121.09 crore, of which the urban population was about 37.71 crore.

 

• Urbanisation increased from 27.81% in Census 2001 to 31.16% in Census 2011, an increase of about 3.35 percentage points.

 

• Maharashtra had the highest urban population in absolute numbers, while among major states Tamil Nadu had the highest percentage of urban population (48.45%) as per Census 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after independence; the theme was 'Our Census, Our Future'.

 

• India's decadal growth rate of population during 2001-2011 was 17.64%, the lowest since independence at that time.

 

NOTE

 

• 25.7% (Option 1): Does not correspond to any official Census 2011 urban population figure.

 

• 49.71% (Option 2): Not the Census 2011 urban share; far higher than the actual figure.

 

• 41.72% (Option 3): Not the Census 2011 urban share; this figure is not an official Census statistic.

question: When was the Smart Cities Mission launched by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India on 25 June 2015, under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. (स्मार्ट सिटीज मिशन — वर्ष 2015)

 

• It is an urban renewal and retrofitting programme aiming to develop 100 cities across the country, making them citizen-friendly and sustainable.

 

• The mission focuses on core infrastructure such as adequate water and power supply, sanitation, efficient urban mobility, robust IT connectivity, e-governance, and a clean and sustainable environment.

 

• It was launched alongside two other missions on the same day: the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cities under the Smart Cities Mission are selected through a 'City Challenge' competition, and implementation is carried out through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) at the city level.

 

• The mission was originally intended to run till 2023, with the deadline for the last batch of cities later extended.

 

NOTE

 

• 2017 (Option 2): Not the launch year; several rounds of city selection continued through 2017, but the mission itself began in 2015.

 

• 2016 (Option 3): Not the launch year of the mission.

 

• 2014 (Option 4): The NDA government took office in 2014, but the Smart Cities Mission was formally launched only in 2015.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution directs the state to provide for a 'Uniform Civil Code'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), states that the State shall endeavour to secure for citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India. (समान नागरिक संहिता — अनुच्छेद 44)

 

• It falls under Part IV of the Constitution, which lays down the Directive Principles of State Policy — these are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

• The objective of Article 44 is to replace the personal laws of different religious communities with a common set of laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption for all citizens.

 

• Goa is currently the only Indian state with a functioning Uniform Civil Code, based on the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 45 deals with provision for early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.

 

• Article 43 relates to a living wage for workers.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 45 (Option 1): Deals with early childhood care and education, not Uniform Civil Code.

 

• Article 43 (Option 2): Deals with a living wage and conditions of work for workers.

 

• Article 42 (Option 4): Deals with provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

question: Which of the following is an award presented for classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalidas Samman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalidas Samman is an award instituted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980, given annually in recognition of outstanding contribution to classical music, classical dance, theatre and plastic arts, on a rotational basis. (कालिदास सम्मान — शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• It is named after the celebrated Sanskrit poet and dramatist Kalidasa, and carries a cash prize along with a citation.

 

• Many eminent classical dancers such as Sonal Mansingh and Birju Maharaj have been honoured with the Kalidas Samman for their contribution to classical dance.

 

• The award is administered by the Ustad Alauddin Khan Sangeet evam Kala Academy, Bhopal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi (National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama), is also a major award recognising excellence in classical dance in India.

 

• India recognises eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Kabir Puraskar (Option 1): Awarded by the Uttar Pradesh government for excellence in Hindustani classical vocal/instrumental music.

 

• Saraswati Samman (Option 2): Given by the K.K. Birla Foundation for an outstanding literary work, not dance.

 

• Jnanpith Award (Option 4): India's highest literary award, given for outstanding contribution to Indian literature.

question: Rahul Srivatsav P became India's 74th Chess Grandmaster with Elo rating of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2500.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rahul Srivatshav Peddi, a chess player from Hyderabad, Telangana, became India's 74th Chess Grandmaster in 2022, achieving the required live Elo rating of 2500. (शतरंज ग्रैंडमास्टर — रेटिंग 2500)

 

• He secured his final GM norm and crossed the 2500 Elo rating mark at the Cattolica Chess Festival 2022, satisfying both requirements for the Grandmaster (GM) title.

 

• The Grandmaster (GM) title, awarded by FIDE (the International Chess Federation), is the highest title a chess player can attain (other than World Champion), requiring three GM norms plus a live rating of at least 2500.

 

• He became one of the youngest Indian players at the time to earn the GM title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster, achieving the title in 1988.

 

• India crossed the milestone of 80+ Grandmasters in the years following 2022, reflecting the country's rapid rise in world chess.

 

NOTE

 

• 2400 (Option 1): This is the threshold rating for the International Master (IM) title, not Grandmaster.

 

• 2000 (Option 3): This roughly corresponds to the Candidate Master (CM) level, far below the GM requirement.

 

• 2200 (Option 4): This roughly corresponds to the FIDE Master (FM) level, not the GM requirement.

question: Which experiment was designed to trace the motion of the earth through the 'luminiferous aether', a theoretical substance necessary for the transmission of light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Michelson and Morley experiment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Michelson-Morley experiment, conducted in 1887 by Albert A. Michelson and Edward W. Morley, was designed to detect the motion of the Earth through the hypothetical 'luminiferous aether'. (माइकलसन-मोर्ले प्रयोग — ईथर का खंडन)

 

• The experiment used an interferometer to compare the speed of light in perpendicular directions, expecting a difference due to Earth's motion through the aether.

 

• The experiment famously produced a 'null result' — no significant difference was detected — which is considered one of the most important negative results in the history of physics.

 

• This null result laid crucial groundwork for Albert Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity (1905), which discarded the concept of the aether altogether and postulated that the speed of light is constant in all inertial frames.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Michelson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1907 for his work on optical precision instruments, including this experiment.

 

• The interferometer used is now known as the Michelson interferometer, still widely used in modern optics and gravitational-wave detectors (e.g., LIGO).

 

NOTE

 

• Maxwell and Hertz experiment (Option 1): James Clerk Maxwell formulated the electromagnetic theory of light; Heinrich Hertz experimentally demonstrated the existence of electromagnetic waves — neither was the aether-drift experiment.

 

• Faraday and Henry experiment (Option 2): Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry are associated with electromagnetic induction, unrelated to the aether experiment.

 

• Marconi and Thomson experiment (Option 4): Guglielmo Marconi pioneered radio transmission; this is not the aether-drift experiment.

question: Which of these was NOT one of the reasons for the break in the five year plans after three consequent five year plans were formulated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gulf war.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the first three Five Year Plans (1951-66), India went through a 'Plan Holiday' from 1966 to 1969, during which no formal Five Year Plan was implemented; instead, three Annual Plans were carried out. (योजना अवकाश — पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं में विराम)

 

• The main reasons for this break were the Indo-Pakistan War of 1965, the subsequent devaluation of the Indian rupee in 1966, and two successive years of severe drought (1965-66 and 1966-67) that caused widespread food shortages.

 

• These factors severely strained the Indian economy and forced planners to shift focus from long-term planning to short-term annual planning.

 

• The Gulf War took place in 1990-91, decades after this Plan Holiday period, and was unrelated to the break in the five year plans of the mid-1960s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74) resumed formal planning after the Plan Holiday, with the objective of 'growth with stability' and self-reliance.

 

• The Gulf War of 1990-91 did trigger a Balance of Payments crisis in India, leading to the 1991 economic liberalisation reforms, but this is a separate historical episode from the 1966-69 Plan Holiday.

 

NOTE

 

• Indo-Pakistan conflict (Option 1): The 1965 war was indeed one of the actual reasons for the Plan Holiday.

 

• Devaluation of domestic currency (Option 2): The 1966 rupee devaluation was indeed one of the actual reasons for the Plan Holiday.

 

• Two successive years of drought (Option 4): The droughts of 1965-66 and 1966-67 were indeed one of the actual reasons for the Plan Holiday.

question: Who founded the East India Association in London?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The East India Association was founded by Dadabhai Naoroji in London in 1866. (ईस्ट इंडिया एसोसिएशन — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• It was formed to discuss and put before the British public and Parliament the grievances and viewpoints of Indians, and to influence public opinion in England in favour of Indian causes.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji is popularly known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and later became the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892).

 

• He is also known for his 'Drain of Wealth' theory, articulated in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which explained the economic exploitation of India under British colonial rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji later became the President of the Indian National Congress three times — 1886, 1893, and 1906.

 

• The East India Association later merged with the London Indian Society to form the National Indian Association, and it played a role in the eventual formation of the Indian National Congress (1885).

 

NOTE

 

• Justice Ranade (Option 1): Mahadev Govind Ranade founded the Prarthana Samaj and the Deccan Education Society, not the East India Association.

 

• Ananda Mohan Bose (Option 2): He founded the Indian Association in Calcutta (1876) along with Surendranath Banerjee.

 

• AO Hume (Option 3): Allan Octavian Hume is credited as a founding figure of the Indian National Congress in 1885, not the East India Association.

question: Which river originates from the southern part of Devarayanadurga hill in Tumkur district, and flows for about 221 km before joining Kaveri?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shimsha river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shimsha River originates at an altitude of about 914 m in the Devarayanadurga hill, in Tumakuru (Tumkur) district, Karnataka. (शिमशा नदी — देवरायनदुर्ग पहाड़ी)

 

• It flows for approximately 221 km, passing through Tumkur, Mandya and Ramanagara districts, before joining the Kaveri (Cauvery) River.

 

• The Shimsha River is a tributary of the Kaveri and is notable for the Shivanasamudra Falls, one of the well-known waterfalls of Karnataka, formed on the Kaveri near its confluence area, as well as for the Shimsha hydro-electric power station.

 

• Devarayanadurga is a hill station near Tumkur, also known for the Yoganarasimha and Bhoganarasimha temples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important tributaries of the Kaveri River include the Hemavati, Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati and Arkavati rivers.

 

• The Kaveri River originates at Talakaveri in the Western Ghats, Kodagu district, Karnataka.

 

NOTE

 

• Girna river (Option 2): A tributary of the Tapi River, flowing through Maharashtra, not connected to Devarayanadurga or the Kaveri.

 

• Ghataprabha river (Option 3): A tributary of the Krishna River, originating in Maharashtra's Western Ghats.

 

• Waghur river (Option 4): A tributary of the Tapi River in Maharashtra, unrelated to Devarayanadurga hill.

question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement concerning public goods?
option_1: Usually, public goods are provided by the government.
option_2: Consumption of public goods by people is rivalrous in nature.
option_3: It is not easy to collect fees for public goods from every individual.
option_4: Public goods are non-excludable in nature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Consumption of public goods by people is rivalrous in nature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Public goods are defined by two key properties: non-rivalry and non-excludability. (सार्वजनिक वस्तुएं — गैर-प्रतिस्पर्धी उपभोग)

 

• Non-rivalrous means that one person's consumption of the good does not reduce its availability for others — for example, national defence or a public park can be 'used' by many people simultaneously without depleting it.

 

• Since consumption of public goods is non-rivalrous, not rivalrous, the statement that it is 'rivalrous in nature' is factually incorrect, making it the answer to this question.

 

• Because public goods are non-excludable, it is difficult to charge individual users a fee (the 'free-rider problem'), which is why they are usually provided by the government rather than private markets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of public goods include national defence, street lighting, lighthouses, and public parks.

 

• Goods that are rivalrous but non-excludable (like ocean fisheries) are called common resources, while goods that are excludable but non-rivalrous (like cable TV) are called club goods.

 

NOTE

 

• Usually, public goods are provided by the government (Option 1): This is a correct statement — governments typically provide public goods due to market failure in their provision.

 

• It is not easy to collect fees for public goods from every individual (Option 3): This is a correct statement, arising from the non-excludability of public goods.

 

• Public goods are non-excludable in nature (Option 4): This is a correct and defining statement about public goods.

question: The first World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship will be organised by ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Sports Council of the Deaf (AISCD) received approval from the International Committee of Sports for the Deaf (ICSD) to host the 1st World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship in India in 2023. (प्रथम विश्व बधिर टी20 क्रिकेट चैंपियनशिप — भारत)

 

• This was the first-ever edition of a World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship, marking a landmark event in cricket for the deaf community globally.

 

• The tournament brought together several national teams of deaf cricketers to compete in the T20 format, organised under the aegis of the ICSD (International Committee of Sports for the Deaf).

 

• India has been an active promoter of deaf cricket, with its national deaf cricket team having achieved notable success in earlier bilateral and multilateral deaf cricket events as well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICSD (International Committee of Sports for the Deaf) is the governing body for deaf sports globally, and also organises the Deaflympics.

 

• India has also hosted/participated in other differently-abled cricket formats, such as Blind Cricket World Cups, organised separately under bodies like the World Blind Cricket Council.

 

NOTE

 

• West Indies (Option 1): Did not organise the first World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship.

 

• Australia (Option 2): Did not organise the first World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship.

 

• England (Option 3): Did not organise the first World Deaf T20 Cricket Championship.

question: White light is an example of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is polychromatic light.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• White light (such as sunlight) is composed of a continuous range of wavelengths covering the entire visible spectrum (roughly violet to red), and is therefore called polychromatic light. (श्वेत प्रकाश — बहुरंगी प्रकाश)

 

• This can be demonstrated by passing white light through a prism, which disperses it into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) — the phenomenon of dispersion.

 

• In contrast, monochromatic light consists of a single wavelength/colour (such as light from a sodium vapour lamp).

 

• Since white light contains many different wavelengths combined together, it fits the definition of polychromatic ('many-coloured') light, not monochromatic light.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A LASER (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation) produces coherent, monochromatic light, unlike ordinary white light.

 

• Polarised light is light in which vibrations are restricted to a single plane; ordinary white light from the sun is generally unpolarised.

 

NOTE

 

• Laser light (Option 1): Laser light is coherent and monochromatic (or near-monochromatic), unlike white light.

 

• Plane polarised light (Option 2): Refers to light vibrating in a single plane, a property unrelated to the number of colours/wavelengths present.

 

• Monochromatic light (Option 3): Refers to light of a single wavelength/colour, the opposite of what white light actually is.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor impacting India's climate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sahara Desert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's climate is influenced by factors such as latitude, altitude, the Himalayas, the surrounding seas/oceans, distance from the sea, relief features and pressure/wind systems (monsoons) — the Sahara Desert, located in North Africa, is not among the recognised factors affecting India's climate. (भारत की जलवायु के कारक — सहारा मरुस्थल शामिल नहीं)

 

• The Himalayan Mountains act as a climatic barrier, blocking cold winds from Central Asia and trapping the monsoon winds, ensuring rainfall in the subcontinent.

 

• The surrounding Indian Ocean, Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal are the source of the moisture-laden monsoon winds that bring seasonal rainfall to India.

 

• The Western Ghats cause orographic rainfall on their windward (western) side, while creating a rain-shadow region on the leeward (eastern) side.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has a 'Monsoon type of climate', characterised by seasonal reversal of winds.

 

• Other factors influencing India's climate include the jet streams, El Nino/La Nina, and western disturbances originating from the Mediterranean region.

 

NOTE

 

• Himalayan Mountains (Option 1): A genuine and major factor shaping India's climate, so it is not the answer.

 

• Indian Ocean (Option 3): A genuine factor, being the source of monsoon moisture, so it is not the answer.

 

• Western Ghats (Option 4): A genuine factor causing regional rainfall variation, so it is not the answer.

question: Indian Council of Historical Research is a captive body of __________, Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Education.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Council of Historical Research (ICHR) was set up in 1972 and functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education, Government of India. (भारतीय ऐतिहासिक अनुसंधान परिषद — शिक्षा मंत्रालय)

 

• ICHR is mandated to give a fillip to historical research in the country and to promote objective and scientific writing of history.

 

• It provides financial assistance for historical research projects, publishes journals (such as the 'Indian Historical Review'), and organises seminars, symposia and conferences.

 

• ICHR is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Education (renamed from the Ministry of Human Resource Development, or HRD, in 2020) also oversees other apex bodies such as the UGC (University Grants Commission) and AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education).

 

• Other similar research councils include the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR) and the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR), both also under the Ministry of Education.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Science and Technology (Option 1): Oversees bodies like DST, DBT and CSIR, not ICHR.

 

• Ministry of Tribal Affairs (Option 2): Deals with tribal welfare matters, not historical research.

 

• Ministry of Culture (Option 4): Oversees bodies like the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and National Archives of India, but ICHR itself falls under the Ministry of Education.

question: Who among the following Indian music composers won the Oscar award in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MM Keeravani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M. M. Keeravani (also known as M. M. Kreem) won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song at the 95th Academy Awards in 2023, for the song 'Naatu Naatu' from the film RRR. (नाटू नाटू — एम एम कीरावाणी)

 

• This made 'Naatu Naatu' the first song from an Indian/Asian film to win the Oscar for Best Original Song.

 

• The song's choreography was by Prem Rakshith, and the lyrics were written by Chandrabose; it was performed on stage at the Oscars ceremony.

 

• RRR, directed by S. S. Rajamouli, thus became a landmark Telugu film to achieve global recognition through this Oscar win.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other notable Oscar-related achievement around the same period was the documentary 'The Elephant Whisperers', which won the Oscar for Best Documentary Short Film in 2023.

 

• Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian to win a competitive Oscar, for Best Costume Design (Gandhi, 1982).

 

NOTE

 

• Mani Sharma (Option 1): A noted Telugu film composer, but did not win an Oscar in 2023.

 

• AR Rahman (Option 2): Previously won two Oscars for 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2009), but did not win in 2023.

 

• Devi Sri Prasad (Option 3): A prominent Telugu film composer, but did not win an Oscar in 2023.

question:
Calculate the NNP (in ₹ crore) at market price from the given data.

Particulars: NDP at factor cost = ₹1,25,250 crore; Net income from abroad = (-) ₹581 crore; Net indirect taxes = ₹18,120 crore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,42,789.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NNP at Market Price (NNPMP) is calculated using the formula: NNPMP = NDP at Factor Cost + Net Indirect Taxes + Net Income from Abroad. (शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — बाजार मूल्य पर गणना)

 

• Substituting the given values: NNPMP = 1,25,250 + 18,120 + (-581).

 

• Step 1: 1,25,250 + 18,120 = 1,43,370 (this gives NNP at market price before adjusting for net income from abroad, i.e., domestic + net indirect taxes).

 

• Step 2: 1,43,370 + (-581) = 1,43,370 - 581 = 1,42,789.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NDP at Factor Cost + Net Indirect Taxes = NDP at Market Price; adding Net Income from Abroad to NDP at Market Price gives NNP at Market Price.

 

• Net Indirect Taxes = Indirect Taxes - Subsidies, and this is the key adjustment used to move from 'factor cost' to 'market price' valuation.

 

NOTE

 

• 1,25,831 (Option 1): Results from an incorrect combination of the given figures, not the correct NNP at market price.

 

• 1,43,951 (Option 3): Results from incorrectly adding the net income from abroad instead of subtracting it (1,43,370 + 581), which is arithmetically wrong.

 

• 1,24,669 (Option 4): Results from an incorrect combination/sign error while applying the formula.

question: Which of the following is NOT a political philosophy of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: Sensitive for the historically disadvantaged groups
option_3: Sensitive to the needs of religious and linguistic minorities
option_4: Non-committal to building a common national identity
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-committal to building a common national identity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution is firmly committed to building a common national identity, through provisions such as a single citizenship, a common set of fundamental rights, and integrative institutions — so describing it as 'non-committal' to this goal is factually incorrect. (भारतीय संविधान का दर्शन — राष्ट्रीय पहचान के प्रति प्रतिबद्ध)

 

• The Constitution's philosophy explicitly aims to forge unity while respecting diversity, as reflected in ideas like 'Unity in Diversity'.

 

• It is sensitive to the concerns of historically disadvantaged groups (through provisions for SCs, STs and OBCs) and to the needs of religious and linguistic minorities (through Articles like 29 and 30).

 

• It is also open to community/group-based values, accommodating personal laws and cultural rights of different communities, while still working towards a shared national identity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution captures this composite philosophy through the words 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic' and the ideals of 'Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity'.

 

• Fraternity, as mentioned in the Preamble, is specifically meant to assure the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation.

 

NOTE

 

• Sensitive for the historically disadvantaged groups (Option 1): This is indeed a genuine feature of the Constitution's philosophy (e.g., reservations, protective provisions).

 

• Open to community values (Option 2): This is indeed a genuine feature, reflected in protections for religious and cultural practices.

 

• Sensitive to the needs of religious and linguistic minorities (Option 3): This is indeed a genuine feature, reflected in Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution.

question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 is applicable to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, passed by Parliament in the Winter Session of 2022, amended the Scheduled Tribes list for Uttar Pradesh. (अनुसूचित जनजाति आदेश संशोधन विधेयक — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The Bill added the 'Gond' community (along with related sub-groups such as Dhuria, Nayak, Ojha, Pathari and Rajgond) to the list of Scheduled Tribes in specific districts of Uttar Pradesh, including Sonbhadra, Chandauli, Mirzapur and Sant Ravidas Nagar.

 

• This amendment enabled members of the Gond community in these UP districts to access the constitutional benefits and reservations available to Scheduled Tribes.

 

• The Bill was part of a set of Constitution (SC/ST) Orders Amendment Bills passed in that session, covering changes for a few different states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Changes to the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes lists of any state require a Constitutional Amendment Bill passed by Parliament, as per Articles 341 and 342 of the Constitution.

 

• The Gond community is one of the largest tribal groups in India, traditionally concentrated in central Indian states such as Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Not the state covered by this particular Second Amendment Bill of 2022.

question: Which of the following folk dances is primarily associated with Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gair.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gair dance is a popular folk dance of Rajasthan, traditionally performed by the Bhil community during festivals like Holi and Janmashtami. (गैर नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• It is performed by men in circular formations, often carrying sticks (danda), moving to the rhythm of drums such as the dhol and algoza, somewhat similar in spirit to the Gujarati Dandiya Raas.

 

• Popular regions for the Gair dance include Udaipur, Dungarpur and Banswara in southern Rajasthan.

 

• Rajasthan has a rich tradition of numerous folk dances beyond Gair, including Ghoomar, Kalbelia, Chari, Bhavai and Terah Taali.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghoomar, performed by women, is perhaps the most iconic folk dance of Rajasthan, especially of the Bhil tribe and Rajput women.

 

• Kalbelia, performed by the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan, is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

NOTE

 

• Tapu (Option 1): A folk dance associated with Uttar Pradesh (Rai/Kanpuriya region and Bundelkhand areas), not Rajasthan.

 

• Dhimsa (Option 3): A tribal folk dance associated with Andhra Pradesh and Odisha (performed by tribes of the Eastern Ghats), not Rajasthan.

 

• Bihu (Option 4): The famous folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bihu festivals, not Rajasthan.

question: What was the theme of the 75th year celebration of the Indian Independence Day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nation First, Always First.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The theme of India's 75th Independence Day (15 August 2021) celebrations was 'Nation First, Always First'. (75वां स्वतंत्रता दिवस — नेशन फर्स्ट, ऑलवेज फर्स्ट)

 

• This 75th anniversary was celebrated as part of the 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav', a series of events initiated by the Government of India to commemorate 75 years of independence and the glorious history of its people, culture and achievements.

 

• The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign, encouraging citizens to hoist the national flag at their homes, was also promoted as part of the broader Amrit Mahotsav celebrations in subsequent years.

 

• The Prime Minister hoisted the national flag at the Red Fort, Delhi, and delivered the customary Independence Day address.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav was officially launched on 12 March 2021, marking the start of a 75-week countdown to the 75th anniversary of independence.

 

• India's Independence Day is celebrated every year on 15 August, commemorating independence from British rule in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• Cultural Development of India (Option 1): Not the official theme of the 75th Independence Day.

 

• The Happiest Place on Earth (Option 3): Not the official theme of the 75th Independence Day.

 

• Women Empowerment (Option 4): Not the official theme of the 75th Independence Day, though women-led development has been a recurring emphasis in government messaging.

question:
Which of the following is true?

A) Fiscal deficit is financed from borrowings.

B) Recovery of loans is a revenue receipt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: The fiscal deficit represents the gap between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts (excluding borrowings); this gap is, by definition, met through borrowings — from the market, RBI, or other sources. (राजकोषीय घाटा — उधार से वित्तपोषित)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: Recovery of loans is classified as a capital receipt, not a revenue receipt, because it reduces government assets/claims (reduces the outstanding loan amount) rather than creating a recurring income stream or a liability.

 

• Revenue receipts are receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce an asset — such as tax revenue and interest/dividend receipts.

 

• Capital receipts, by contrast, either create a liability (like market borrowings) or reduce an asset (like recovery of loans or disinvestment proceeds).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's fiscal deficit target and actual figures are announced every year as part of the Union Budget, usually expressed as a percentage of GDP.

 

• Other examples of capital receipts include disinvestment of public sector shares and market borrowings/loans from the public.

 

NOTE

 

• Only B (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement B is false (recovery of loans is a capital receipt, not revenue receipt), while Statement A is true.

 

• Neither A nor B (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement A is in fact true.

 

• Both A and B (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement B is false.

question: Which of the following is a correct expression?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net investment = Gross investment – Depreciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross investment refers to the total expenditure on capital goods (like machinery and buildings) in an economy during a given period, without adjusting for wear and tear. (शुद्ध निवेश — सकल निवेश घटा मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Depreciation (also called consumption of fixed capital) refers to the loss in value of capital assets due to normal wear and tear, obsolescence, and the passage of time.

 

• Net investment is the actual addition to the capital stock of the economy, obtained after deducting depreciation from gross investment: Net Investment = Gross Investment - Depreciation.

 

• Rearranging this formula also gives: Gross Investment = Net Investment + Depreciation, and Depreciation = Gross Investment - Net Investment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This same 'gross minus depreciation equals net' relationship also applies to national income aggregates — e.g., NNP = GNP - Depreciation, and NDP = GDP - Depreciation.

 

• Depreciation is estimated using conventional accounting methods and is a deduction used while moving from 'Gross' to 'Net' concepts in national income accounting.

 

NOTE

 

• Depreciation = Net investment – Gross investment (Option 1): Incorrect; this would give a negative value since gross investment is normally greater than net investment. The correct relation is Depreciation = Gross Investment - Net Investment.

 

• Gross investment = Net investment – Depreciation (Option 2): Incorrect; this reverses the correct relationship (it would understate gross investment).

 

• Net investment = Gross investment + Depreciation (Option 4): Incorrect; adding depreciation (instead of subtracting it) would overstate net investment.

question: Which Indian Cricketer was the special guest at the Melbourne Indian Film Festival in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kapil Dev.

• The 2022 edition of IFFM was notable for being held 'on ground' (in-person) after disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic in previous years.

 

• Kapil Dev famously captained the Indian cricket team to its first World Cup victory in 1983, a feat later dramatized in the Bollywood film '83', which added to the thematic connection with his presence at a film festival.

 

• The Indian Film Festival of Melbourne is one of the largest festivals dedicated to Indian cinema outside India, celebrating Bollywood and regional Indian films.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kapil Dev was honoured with the Padma Shri (1982) and Padma Bhushan (1991), and was named the 'Indian Cricketer of the Century' by Wisden in 2002.

• MS Dhoni (Option 2): Was not the special guest at IFFM 2022.

question: Ghiyasuddin Balban introduced the customs of 'Sijda' and 'Paibos' as normal forms of salutations to the king as a part of __________ etiquette.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Court.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban, the powerful Delhi Sultanate ruler of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, introduced the ceremonies of 'Sijda' (prostration before the king) and 'Paibos' (kissing the monarch's feet) as part of strict court etiquette. (सिजदा और पैबोस — बलबन का दरबारी शिष्टाचार)

 

• Balban sought to enhance the prestige, dignity and authority of the crown by enforcing elaborate court ceremonials and rituals, distancing the monarchy from the nobility.

 

• He propagated the theory of kingship as the 'Shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) on earth, and organized an elaborate and disciplined court to reflect this exalted status.

 

• He also introduced Persian festivals like Nauroz at his court and maintained a rigid, disciplined administrative and military structure, including the espionage system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balban is also known for crushing the power of the 'Chahalgani' (the Forty), a group of powerful Turkish nobles who had earlier dominated the Sultanate's politics.

 

• He ruled from 1266 to 1287 CE and is credited with strengthening the military and administrative apparatus of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

NOTE

 

• Army (Option 1): Sijda and Paibos were ceremonial court customs of salutation, not army/military customs.

 

• Family (Option 2): These customs applied to courtiers and nobles at the royal court, not to family relations.

 

• Religious (Option 3): These were royal court ceremonial customs, not religious rituals.

question: An excessive amount of cadmium in the human body causes:
solution_text:
The correct answer is itai-itai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Itai-itai disease is caused by chronic cadmium poisoning, and was first identified in Toyama Prefecture, Japan, in the early 20th century, resulting from cadmium-contaminated water used for irrigation near mining operations. (इटाई-इटाई रोग — कैडमियम विषाक्तता)

 

• The name 'itai-itai' literally means 'it hurts, it hurts' in Japanese, referring to the severe pain in the joints and spine caused by the disease.

 

• Cadmium poisoning leads to softening of bones and kidney failure, as cadmium disrupts calcium metabolism in the body.

 

• It is considered one of the 'Four Big Pollution Diseases of Japan', alongside Minamata disease, the second Minamata disease, and Yokkaichi asthma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Minamata disease, by contrast, is caused by methylmercury poisoning, first identified in Minamata, Japan, due to industrial wastewater discharge.

 

• Other heavy metal-related health disorders include lead poisoning (plumbism) and arsenic poisoning (arsenicosis), both of which have their own distinct symptoms.

 

NOTE

 

• minamata (Option 1): This disease is caused by mercury (methylmercury) poisoning, not cadmium.

 

• anaemia (Option 2): A blood disorder generally linked to iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, not specifically a hallmark disease of cadmium poisoning.

 

• alzima (Option 3): Not a recognized medical condition or disease name associated with cadmium poisoning.
